question: Your extraction system reads shipping manifests and fills a JSON schema for each one. On the synchronous Claude API, Claude calls a lookup_port_code tool, your code returns the code, and Claude then completes the record. After the team moved the nightly run to the Message Batches API, most responses ended with stop_reason "tool_use" and no completed record. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The batch API cannot execute the port lookup mid-request and send its result back to Claude within the same request.
options.reason: The guide states that the batch API does not support multi-turn tool calling. Each request therefore stops at the tool call without a finished record.

options.text: The 24-hour processing window ran out before the port codes arrived, so the batch service cut off each extraction before Claude could finish it.
options.reason: The 24-hour window is the maximum processing time, and the responses did come back. The real cause is that the batch API never returns tool results to Claude mid-request.

options.text: The 50% cost savings come from a smaller model in the batch API that cannot produce the complete JSON schema output.
options.reason: The guide names the 50% cost savings but no reduced model. The responses stopped because the batch API has no multi-turn tool calling.

options.text: Duplicate custom_id values made the batch service match each response to the wrong manifest request in the results.
options.reason: The guide describes custom_id as the field that correlates requests with responses. A correlation error would mismatch records, but it would not make responses stop at a tool call.
